transcription.tex: \textbf{Lines and planes}\par 1. Write vector and Cartesian equations of lines.\par 2. Describe a plane using two directions or a normal vector.\par 3. Use scalar products to find angles.
\textbf{Geometry in three dimensions}\par 4. Find intersections and distinguish skew lines.\par 5. Calculate shortest distances.\par 6. Reflect points and lines in planes.

slides.title: Vector equation of a straight line in 3D

transcription.tex: A vector equation describes every point on a straight line.\[\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}3\\0\\-2\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}\]Find the points for \(\lambda=0,1,2,-1\).

The first vector locates a fixed point. The second gives the direction.\par Changing \(\lambda\) moves along the line in either direction.\par The direction vector is non-zero.\[\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf b\]

transcription.tex: For a line \(\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf b\):\[x=a_1+\lambda b_1,\ y=a_2+\lambda b_2,\ z=a_3+\lambda b_3\]

transcription.tex: 1. Use the definition of scalar product to prove commutativity.

2a. Show the three projection identities.\par 2b. Hence prove distributivity.

\[\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf b+\mathbf c)=|\mathbf a|\,PQ\]\[\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b=|\mathbf a|\,PR\]\[\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf c=|\mathbf a|\,RQ\]Each follows by resolving the second vector along \(\mathbf a\).
\[PQ=PR+RQ\]\[\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf b+\mathbf c)=|\mathbf a|(PR+RQ)\]\[=\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b+\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf c\]

transcription.tex: 13. A regular tetrahedron has vertices \(A(0,0,0),\) \(B(0,1,1),\) \(C(1,1,0),\) \(D(1,0,1)\). Show the angle between adjacent faces is \(\cos^{-1}(1/3)\).

Let \(E\) be the midpoint of \(AD\). Both \(EB\) and \(EC\) are perpendicular to \(AD\).\[E=(1/2,0,1/2)\]\[EB=(-1/2,1,1/2)\]\[EC=(1/2,1,-1/2)\]\[\cos\angle BEC=\frac{1/2}{\sqrt{3/2}\sqrt{3/2}}=\frac13\]Regularity gives the same angle at every edge.

transcription.tex: 12. Reflect the line\[\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}2\\-1\\2\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}4\\-3\\4\end{pmatrix}\]in the plane \(\mathbf r\cdot(1,-1,-1)=4\).
